brief: BofA reports from the 2026 WNA Symposium, remaining constructive on nuclear energy and naming CEG, TLN, VST (power), CCJ, OKLO (vendors) and CCJ, STDN (fuel cycle) as Buy-rated exposure. WNA's COP28 goal to triple global nuclear capacity from 392GWe (2020) to near 1,200GWe by 2050 is now tracked against current aggregate country targets of 1,457GW by 2050, a near-quadrupling. Panelists tied build-out success to policy, standardization and financing, with end users like Amazon and Equinix backing developers such as X-Energy, Oklo and Radiant. In the US, a May 2025 Executive Order calling for 10 large reactors under construction by 2030 has produced a $17.5bn DOE loan program with seven counterparty letters of intent; some attendees were hopeful for 1-2 site announcements by the midterms. Cameco's CEO framed uranium mining, not conversion or enrichment, as the binding bottleneck, since deposits are non-reproducible and mine lead times run up to 20 years. BofA maintains a bullish U3O8 forecast, peaking at $129.80/lb in 2027 before easing to an $84.75/lb long-term price below current spot, as conversion and enrichment markets sit near all-time highs.
